1.explanation: Prism processes the rules in the order they are declared. The `inline` rule (which includes patterns for backtick‐delimited text, italics, bold, inline literals, etc.) comes before the `link` rule, so a backtick‐wrapped hyperlink target is consumed entirely by `inline` and never reaches the `link` matcher. As a result, links like `<https://…>`_ are never detected. Moving or refining the `link` patterns to run before—or give precedence over—the general `inline` pattern will allow explicit hyperlink targets to be tokenized correctly.
1.bug_scenario: In Prism’s reST language plugin, an inline code snippet combining backtick‐delimited text and an explicit hyperlink target—``` `ALTER ROLE <https://…>`_ ```—is not being tokenized as a link followed by an inline‐literal. Instead, the entire snippet is treated as italic text. When separated onto two lines, the link and the literal are highlighted correctly, but on one line the “inline” rule greedily matches the whole backtick‐delimited segment, preventing the “link” rule from ever running.

2.explanation:
All of the reST inline markup is driven by the regex token definitions inside Prism.languages.rest. In particular:

- The "inline" token’s big regex is too greedy and absorbs the `<…>` link syntax (and the trailing underscore) before the separate link‐recognition patterns can run.

- The "link" token array, which should detect backtick‐delimited interpreted‐text followed by an underscore, is never reached when the inline regex has already matched.

To fix the bug, the inline and link regexes in components/prism-rest.js must be adjusted so that link syntax (`…`_ ) and inline‐literal syntax (``…``) are recognized first, before falling back to italic/bold matches.
2.bug_scenario:
When a reST inline link and inline‐literal appear on the same line—e.g.

  `ALTER ROLE <https://www.postgresql.org/docs/12/sql-alterrole.html>`_ or ``ALTER_ROLE``

Prism’s rest definition fails to recognize the link and the double‐backtick literal, and instead treats the whole span as italic. When the same markup is split across two lines it highlights correctly.
